sources.snippet: This raises a more fundamental question: how to design a simple, elegant and efficient VLA that directly maps vision and language to actions for execution-level manipulation, without centering on a large language model? Figure 2: From LLM-centric VLA to TurboVLA.

sources.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX ...
sources.snippet: Vision-language-action (VLA) models commonly adopt an LLM-centric V to L to A pathway, where visual observations are projected into the representation space of a large language model before being decoded into robot actions. Although effective, this design incurs substantial computation and memory overhead at every policy invocation.
